parsed.explanation: The notation defines π(s) only for finite prime-sets, so Claim 3.2's inference 'Hence π(T) ∈ S_∞' is valid only for finite T, while its statement and hypothesis (iii) are unrestricted. Infinite minimal transversals of a family of finite sets do exist (e.g. {{0,n}: n≥1} has the minimal transversal ℕ∖{0}), so the case is not vacuous. In Step 4, part (a)'s Zorn argument yields a minimal transversal T of the infinite set I∪Z_ω with no independent finiteness; the text then applies (iii) to get T ∈ 𝒞 and only afterward says 'Since T is finite' — finiteness derived from the very membership whose proof fails for infinite T. Case A's use of (iii) is safe (T ⊆ finite I∪Z_s), but the process runs forever and the final contradiction in (c) needs the unverified case. Nothing else in the write-up proves finiteness of ℳ (Lemmas A–D are disclaimed as intuition). Gap is real and load-bearing for the lower_bound/finiteness obligation.
